The line-regulation failure (0.1145 V/V against a 0.029 limit, about 4x over) points at the self-bias mirror. Of the listed sensitivities, M4 has by far the largest effect (-5.84% for +20%), which makes it the top suspect. Its drain sits at 0.582 V while its mirror partner M3 is at 0.765 V, so its current is more exposed to supply-dependent channel-length modulation. Mst1 and Mst2 (the startup pair) are the next most influential, since their current feeds the same bias node. The sensitivities are small, so this is a ranking rather than proof. The fault is most likely a wrong M4 size or length that breaks its matching to M3.

{"ranking": ["M4", "Mst1", "Mst2"], "fault": "M4 (PMOS mirror leg feeding node a) is mis-sized relative to its mirror partner M3, so its drain voltage and channel-length modulation mismatch the diode-connected M3. This makes the bias current supply-dependent and drives line_reg far above spec; restoring M4 to the matched sizing (matching M3's W/L and mirror topology) should fix it."}
